source.title: An Inclusive Foundation Model for Generalizable Cytogenetics in Precision Oncology
source.authors: Chang-Chun Yang; Wei-Qian Dai; Yi-Lan Zhang; Siyuan Chen; Jingdong Hu; Junkai Su; Yuxuan Chen; Ao Xu; Na Li; Xin Gao; Y. Yu

record.file_problem: The provided text includes the abstract, main results, discussion, and references, but not the Methods section or supplementary material; it refers to Extended Data Fig. 1 without supplying the figure.
record.tranche_reason: Reports a data-scaling result for CHROMA, a visual foundation model pretrained on chromosome images, extending scaling-law evidence beyond text pretraining.
record.gate_note: The only result bearing on the claim is the stated relationship between pretraining data size and performance. The downstream classification results do not test the claim versions. The text does not provide the underlying scaling curve or its fit details.
record.test_reason: The study reports one result of its own: CHROMA's masked-autoencoder pretraining on chromosome images 'demonstrated strong alignment with data scaling laws' (R² = 0.89, Extended Data Fig. 1). That bears on V5 (power-law form beyond text) in an image-pretraining setting. The available text does not give the measure, the functional form, the data-size range or the curve, so the result cannot be read against V5.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct, with one correction: scaling is a single side remark in the paper. The authors' main conclusion is that CHROMA outperforms SL, contrastive SSL and MAE baselines across numerical, stable-structural and unstable-structural abnormality detection. It is also more label-efficient and reliable with risk control. The scaling sentence only says pretraining 'demonstrated strong alignment with data scaling laws' (R² = 0.89).
record.recipe_differences: This study uses self-supervised masked-autoencoder pretraining on chromosome images and examines scaling with data size, rather than language-model loss scaling across parameters, tokens, and compute.

fits_no_version.finding: Fine-tuning label-efficiency curves: CHROMA reaches F1 0.86 with about 35% less data, and AUROC about 0.86 with about 45% fewer labelled abnormal instances than the baselines.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Domain-specific self-supervised pretraining improves downstream label efficiency relative to supervised and generic SSL baselines (not a scaling-law claim).

record.problems: The scaling evidence is summarized only by R² = 0.89 and a statement of consistent gains; the curve, fit method, exponent, data-size range, and uncertainty for this result are not given in the provided text.
record.rows_left_out: The remaining reported results concern chromosome classification and are not results on the claim versions. No other claim-relevant scaling result was stated.

untested.parts: Explicit power-law form and exponent for image pretraining; scaling with parameters or compute; video, repeated data, fine-tuning and transfer regimes.
Extrapolation from small runs; not studied.
Architecture shape at fixed parameter count; not studied.
Downstream performance as a function of pretraining scale; the label-efficiency curves vary fine-tuning labels, not pretraining scale.

missing.what: Extended Data Fig. 1 data-scaling curve: data sizes, measure, fitted functional form, exponent and fit method behind the R² = 0.89.
missing.locator: Results, Workflow and datasets; Extended Data Fig. 1; Methods (not in provided text)

record.verdict_notes: No verdict is given because the only linked row cannot be read against V5. The scaling-law reference cites Kaplan et al. A reader with the Methods and Extended Data Fig. 1 could re-assess it. If the figure shows a power-law fit of pretraining loss against data size, r1 would become 'observed' and V5 would get 'supports' for chromosome-image MAE data scaling.

rows.subject: CHROMA

rows.operation_detail: Evaluated pretraining performance as data size increased

conditions.value: increasing pretraining data size; specific sizes not stated

rows.measure: Alignment with data scaling laws / pretraining performance as data size increased
rows.value: R² = 0.89; consistent performance gains as data size increased
rows.locator: Results, Workflow and datasets; Extended Data Fig. 1
rows.note: The text calls the alignment strong but does not specify the fitted functional form, exponent, or underlying curve values.
rows.check: State 'partial' is unjustified: the text shows no weaker-than-expected effect. It also contradicts the record's 'supports' label. The measure is unspecified ('pretraining performance', possibly reconstruction loss or something else). The fitted form (power law or other), exponent, data-size range and curve are not given, and Extended Data Fig. 1 is absent. An R² of 0.89 against an unstated law cannot show whether a power law holds.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
